patient.chief_complaint: Thunderclap headache onset 2 hours ago, vomiting, neck pain
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Harris is a 43-year-old woman on oral contraceptives and a smoker presenting with sudden onset severe headache 2 hours before arrival. She was at her computer when she experienced an instantaneous explosive headache she rates 10/10, unlike any previous headache. She immediately felt nauseated and vomited twice. She called her partner who brought her to the emergency department. She describes the pain as global, throbbing, and accompanied by photophobia and stiff neck that began about 30 minutes after the headache onset. She has not lost consciousness. She denies prior episodes of similar headache. She reports occasional mild headaches that she treats with ibuprofen. She has been on oral contraceptives for 8 years and smokes. She has no known hypertension but has never been formally evaluated. Her blood pressure in the ED is markedly elevated. She denies focal weakness, vision loss, or speech difficulty. She is cooperative but clearly in significant distress from the headache. She denies recent trauma or exertion at time of onset - it occurred at rest.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; significant pain distress; photophobic
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 4mm; EOM fully intact; no ptosis; no papilledema
neurological_exam.additional: Nuchal rigidity present; Kernig sign positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Moderate hyperdense blood in suprasellar cistern and interpeduncular fossa

ct.impression: 1. Moderate subarachnoid hemorrhage with hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures; Fisher grade 3. 2. No acute hydrocephalus. 3. No parenchymal hematoma. CT angiography of the head and neck recommended.
recommended_actions: CT angiography of the head and neck recommended

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 16.2 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 144 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.11 ng/mL (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 26 cmH2O. WBC: N/A (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 178 mg/dL. Glucose: 72 mg/dL (serum 144, ratio 0.50) (ratio 0.50). Xanthochromia: Present on spectrophotometry.

ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia, rate 114. Diffuse T-wave inversions V1–V5. QTc 478 ms, mildly prolonged. No ST-segment elevation. No pathological Q waves. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Irregular saccular aneurysm 5.8 x 4.6 mm with asymmetric lobulation

output.impression: 1. Saccular aneurysm at the anterior communicating artery, 5.8 x 4.6 mm, with asymmetric lobulation. 2. No additional intracranial aneurysm. Conventional DSA recommended for definitive characterization.
recommended_actions: Conventional DSA recommended for definitive characterization

output.proposed: Continue ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate (patient requesting to continue)
contraindications: Oral contraceptives increase hypertension and thrombotic risk
Thrombotic complications can occur post-SAH coiling with OCP use
warnings: Recommend discontinuation of OCP given intracranial hemorrhage and hypertension

output.impression: Day 5 TCD: bilateral ACA mean flow velocity mildly elevated (122–134 cm/s, Lindegaard ratio 3.4–3.6); bilateral MCA borderline (108–118 cm/s); basilar normal. Findings are consistent with mild bilateral ACA vasospasm. Clinical correlation recommended.
Normal transthoracic echocardiogram. LVEF 56%. No regional wall motion abnormality. No significant valvular disease.

output.query: Oral contraceptive use intracranial aneurysm risk subarachnoid hemorrhage

results.finding: OCP use associated with modest increased risk of SAH (OR 1.5-2.0) in some studies
Combined OCP + smoking significantly increases stroke and aneurysm rupture risk
OCP should be discontinued post-SAH; alternative contraception recommended

output.summary: Combined oral contraceptive use has been associated with a modest increased risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage in some epidemiological studies, particularly in combination with tobacco use. After intracranial hemorrhage, current evidence supports considering discontinuation of combined estrogen–progestin contraception and transition to alternative methods; clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: CT perfusion: mild bilateral anterior circulation CBF reduction (32–38 mL/100g/min); CBV preserved bilaterally; TTP mildly prolonged bilaterally. No established infarction. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from anterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CTA shows saccular aneurysm; CSF bloody with xanthochromia
Hypertension likely contributed to aneurysm rupture; BP 188/112
No venous sinus occlusion on CTA; hemorrhage is SAH not CVT pattern

optimal_actions.action: CT head - confirm SAH Fisher grade 3

optimal_actions.expected_finding: OCP should be discontinued in SAH context

optimal_actions.action: Counsel patient on OCP discontinuation and smoking cessation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: OCP + smoking increases SAH/aneurysm rupture risk

critical_actions: CT and CTA urgently for SAH confirmation and aneurysm identification
Discontinue OCP - increases thrombotic risk and may have contributed to SAH
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue oral contraceptives after SAH diagnosis
Do not give ibuprofen or NSAIDs post-SAH
Do not miss OCP as a modifiable SAH risk factor
key_reasoning_points: OCP use combined with smoking is a modifiable risk factor combination associated with increased aneurysm rupture risk
Young woman with no hypertension history presenting with thunderclap headache - SAH must be first consideration
AComA is the most common aneurysm location and correlates with basal cistern blood distribution
OCP should be discontinued post-SAH - both thrombotic risk from OCP and hypertension risk are relevant
Fisher grade 3 SAH carries higher vasospasm risk - monitor TCD daily from day 4-14
Smoking cessation is a critical secondary prevention measure for cerebrovascular disease

red_herrings.data_point: Oral contraceptive use (ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate) in a 43-year-old woman with new hypertension
red_herrings.intended_effect: The combination of OCP use, markedly elevated BP (188/112), and thunderclap headache may redirect the clinician toward OCP-related cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT) as the primary diagnosis rather than aneurysmal SAH
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: OCP use is a risk factor for CVT but also a modifiable risk factor for aneurysm rupture. CT shows classic SAH distribution (basal cisterns, Sylvian fissures) not the cortical venous pattern of CVT. CTA shows no venous occlusion and confirms AComA aneurysm. The primary diagnosis is aneurysmal SAH; OCP should be discontinued as a secondary prevention measure.
